threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Tube' instead of the 'Overground' and get baffled when people assume you know the bus routes by heart.
Last night on the 196 bus, a guy sat across from me rummaged through a bag of fried chicken like it was gold. He offered me a wing like we were old mates.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a cat calmly perched on a bus stop sign, waiting for its owner who was busy chatting on the corner. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a corner café where every table has a board game. You can sip your coffee while rolling dice and claiming territories.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they weave through the BART delays without breaking a sweat, while newcomers stare at their phones confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a pigeon hitching a ride on the back of a Muni bus today. That bird looked like it owned the place—only in SF, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can see all the sights at a leisurely pace, but locals know rush hour means watching the clock, not the architecture.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their hesitation at ordering 'café con leche'—they always ask for 'just coffee' first.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it Dalston Junction instead of just Junction. No local ever says the full name, it’s like a badge of honour.
Last night on the 196, a guy serenaded a confused pigeon at the stop. The pigeon just stood there, judging him silently. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I found a stray cat lounging on my windowsill, sunbathing like it owned the place. That’s Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg would you find a currywurst stand open at 3 AM, serving up late-night snacks while the techno from the clubs spills onto the street.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local would know to avoid 24th St. BART when there's a delay; they reroute through the alleys to dodge the chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy trying to convince the driver to let him on while in mid-conversation with his dog. Dog seemed more persuasive than he was.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think it’s normal to only eat pinchos at 10 PM. Most locals stick to a proper dinner around 9, and we prefer a quieter vibe over the late-night frenzy.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewildered look when they see the 'Fira de Sant Medir' parade; locals know to avoid the area that day.
